speaker: provenzano
text: So I have a proclamation here for International Women's Day. Before I start, I just want to thank you and recognize all the tremendous women in our community who are doing great work. And obviously the woman who sit with us here on council, Councillor Hilsinger, Councillor Bessel-Allen and Councillor Hollingsworth, who is not with us tonight and the leadership we have here at city hall, our clerk and our deputy clerk who are with us tonight and my mother and my wife and my sister. And of course my three little girls, Isla, Chloe and Alice. I think they might be watching right now. So I wanted to say their names for that. So whereas the first International Women's Day was celebrated 110 years ago, International Women's Day belongs to all communities everywhere. Governments, companies, charities, educational institutes, networks, associations, the media and more. Whether through a global conference, community gathering, classroom lesson or dinner table conversation, we can all play a meaningful role and present pressing for gender balance. Whereas the COVID-19 pandemic is having a disproportionate economic impact on women and existing systemic inequalities have been further exacerbated by recent shutdown measures, resulting with some economists are calling a she session as more women have lost their jobs and fewer women than men are regaining employment. The pandemic experience has been especially challenging for already vulnerable groups, including racialized, indigenous and low-income women, single mothers, newcomers and women with disabilities. Whereas women's labor force participation is at a record low, decades of progress towards gender equality are at stake. We need to take a hard look at the challenges facing women and plan for recovery with women at the table with a gender and diversity lens on strategies, programs and policies. Whereas a challenged world is an alert world, one that supports women's safety, economic empowerment and prosperity and extremely important to our organization, community, province and country. You choose to challenge to support International Women's Day. And therefore I Christian Provenzano as Mayor of Sault Ste. Marie do hereby proclaim and recognize March 8th, 2021 as International Women's Day here in Sault Ste. Marie. And I urge all of our citizens to challenge and call it gender bias and inequality. From challenge comes change. Thank you.

speaker: racheltyczinski
text: And under agenda item 5.2, a proclamation for World Water Day 2021.

speaker: provenzano
text: Thank you, I have a proclamation. Whereas since 1992, the United Nations designates March 22nd every year around the globe is World Water Day. Whereas the theme of World Water Day 2021 is valuing water, aligned with the United Nations Decade for Action with the water bowl as a top strategic priority. The aim of this goal is to bring greater focus to freshwater around the world. And whereas in Sault Ste. Marie, we are uniquely located at this nexus of Lake Superior and Lake Huron connected by the St. Mary's River and share international waterways. The Great Lakes combined comprise nearly 20% of the world's freshwater and only 0.3% is accessible to all humankind. Whereas World Water Day provides an opportunity to make a difference in our community. We want to raise awareness of water in our region through education, science, research, culture and creative mediums to learn deeply together as a community about our waterways and find actions each of us can take to protect and restore the amazing source of freshwater all around us. Whereas Sault Ste. Marie wishes to acknowledge and respect the importance of protecting this freshwater for today and for generations to come. And therefore I, Christian Provenzanos, Mayor of the City of Sault Ste. Marie do hereby proclaim March 22nd, 2021 as World Water Day here in Sault Ste. Marie. Thank you.

speaker: racheltyczinski
text: So moving to agenda item 8.1, a motion by Councilors Dufour and Christian, whereas city council has identified building and by-law as a pivotal area of focus to improve the approach in dealing with derelict and vacant buildings. And whereas city council has established a task force to effect those needed improvements in our system. And whereas the building and by-law task force has identified among other suggestions, the amendment to the city's property standards by-law 2012-9 to improve part seven of the by-law dealing with vacant or damaged buildings. And whereas these amendments would allow for increased enforcement as a tool that would help to curb the spread of derelict buildings. And whereas the building department writes orders for compliance and where compliance is not achieved, the legal department is responsible for the required court proceedings. And whereas the implementation of the integrated municipal enforcement team, IMET, has added to court proceedings being conducted by the legal department. And whereas the capacity of the legal department has been a pinch point for prosecuting charges and drafting the amended vacant building section of the property standards by-law. And whereas the legal department had presented information showing that costs are saved when keeping legal work in-house rather than seeking assistance from contracted outside council. Now therefore be it resolved that the legal department be asked to prepare a report outlining how an additional lawyer could be funded from a corresponding decrease in the contracted legal council budget in 2021 with adjustments for 2022 made as necessary during budget deliberations.

speaker: provenzano
text: That's due for, I'm going to start with you because this is your motion and we'll go from there.

text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mayor. Just as a point of background for the public, I know that the rest of city council is very well familiar, but part of what this is looking to address here is the rise and the continued presence of vacant buildings, particularly in areas of our city that have experienced declining or stagnating assessment values. Many of these buildings, I know anecdotally, having been in the construction industry and driving around a lot, they've been sitting vacant for years. You know, and quite frankly, I think the message from this council needs to be that they need to be developed or they need to be demolished. And in order for that message to come across loud and clear, us as a city council need to be willing to properly resource the mechanisms that see to it that this happens. Obviously during budget time, city council didn't see fit to add this to the general levy, although I don't necessarily agree with the decision. Certainly that's council's prerogative, but I do believe that this is a very critical investment that needs to be made now, which is why it's coming back in a different form with a different funding mechanism. Again, anecdotally, I've seen a lot of a lot of really interesting sales in the real estate market over the last few months, you know, several perpetual vacant buildings changing hands, being purchased sometimes by out of town buyers and for prices that are fairly high. I think now more than ever, this council needs to ensure that our stable of vacant buildings in the city is not growing, that these are being properly built dealt with in the sense that the cost to the neighborhoods, the cost to the city budget is being reflected in the cost of owning these buildings. They really do need to be developed or demolished. And I think that this is a very responsible way to the taxpayer to help fund one of those necessary investments. So I look forward to our discussion tonight, Mr. Mayor. Thank you.
